name: Trio v1.0.2
body:
# Trio v1.0.2 ![trio](https://raw.githubusercontent.com/nightscout/trio-docs/e78591c461fa022ef7426a2ca65996f0899546da/docs/favicon.ico) This release ships an updated driver for Libre 3/3+, brings in a large round of pump and sensor driver updates, fixes alarms that warned too early, a basal rate that showed the wrong number, and a handful of other small issues. > [!IMPORTANT] > **Using a FreeStyle Libre 3 or 3+? You must pair your sensor again after updating.** > Trio has switched to an updated Libre driver. It cannot carry your old pairing over, so your sensor will stop sending readings until you re-pair it. > **You do not need a new sensor.** Keep the one you are wearing. Open **Settings → CGM → FreeStyle Libre 3 / 3+**, tap **Pair New Sensor**, and scan the sensor with your phone, exactly like you did the very first time. > Do this as soon as you update. Until you do, Trio has no glucose data and cannot loop. --- ## What's Changed At A Glance - **Not-looping alerts warn you sooner** – Trio now nudges you at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 minutes, and sounds a critical alarm at 120. Before, you got one critical alarm at 20 minutes and nothing else - **New alarm sound defaults for new installs** – critical alarms make a sound, the quieter two types stay silent. If you already have Trio, your own alarm settings are untouched - **Updated driver for Libre 3 / 3+** – more reliable pairing, and a nearby Libre sensor can no longer be paired by mistake. Re-pairing is required, see above - **The basal rate on the Home chart is correct again** – it no longer shows a temp basal that was already cancelled, and it tells you when delivery is suspended - **Omnipod pairing in a household with several pods** – Trio now only counts pods that are actually ready to pair, so you no longer get a "too many pods found" error - **Medtrum patch fixes** – no more crash when a patch reports a halted delivery, and Trio stops you priming before the patch is filled - **Eversense fixes** – readings no longer stop unexpectedly, the sensor reconnects after you restart Trio, and more useful data is sent to Eversense DMS - **AccuChek and Eversense show warm-up and expiry** – you can see on the Home screen when a sensor is warming up and when it runs out - **Calibrations now show as fingersticks** – a calibration you enter is saved as a manual reading with the red drop on the chart, not as a sensor reading - **Dexcom sensor states can go to Nightscout** – an off-by-default switch posts a note like "CGM: sensorFailed" when a G6 or G7 reading has no usable glucose --- ## FreeStyle Libre 3 / 3+ Trio's Libre support moved to a new driver, RoundWhiteDiscKit, together with the current version of LibreLoop ([#1609](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1609)). **You must pair your sensor again after updating** – see the note at the top. Nothing else about Libre changes for you. What the new driver brings: - **Pairing is more reliable.** It uses a proper app credential, which Trio checks before it is used. - **The right sensor gets paired.** Trio now matches the sensor from your NFC scan by its Bluetooth address, so another Libre-family sensor nearby – a Lingo, for example – can no longer win the scan. - **More information when something goes wrong.** Settings → Debug Info now shows your sensor's security version and region. Libre 3 / 3+ support is still marked **(Beta)** in Trio. It has been tested on a U.S. and EU Libre 3 Plus. --- ## Alarms - **Not-looping alerts now escalate** ([#1552](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1552)). Trio used to go straight to one critical alarm at 20 minutes. Now you get a gentler nudge at 20, 40, 60, 80 and 100 minutes, and a critical alarm at 120 minutes. All six are handed to iOS up front, so the warnings keep coming even if iOS puts Trio to sleep. Any successful loop clears them. - **New sound defaults, for new installs only.** On a fresh install, Critical alarms play a sound and Time-Sensitive and Normal alarms are silent. **If you already have Trio installed, your alarm settings are left exactly as you set them.** --- ## Pumps ### Omnipod - **Pairing in a house with more than one pod user.** Trio now counts only pods that are actually candidates for pairing, so the "too many pods found" error is gone. - **Keep-alive stays out of the background.** The "When Open" keep-alive timer no longer runs while Trio is in the background, even if your CGM wakes the app up. - **Silence Pod end time.** Picking a time that has already passed no longer hangs the screen. - **Known pods reconnect more simply**, with one automatic retry if the pod drops the link. Pod pairing and pod end are now recorded as pump events. ### Medtrum - **Priming is blocked until the patch is filled**, and the priming screen now shows the reservoir level. - **Trio will not connect to the wrong base**, and patch states are checked properly rather than guessed at. ### Dana - Temp basal rates are rounded to two decimal places, and the pump keeps a heartbeat during Continuous mode. --- ## Sensors ### Eversense A large driver update ([#1593](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1593)): - **Readings no longer stop unexpectedly**, and crashes during state changes are fixed. - **Your transmitter reconnects after you restart Trio**, instead of needing to be set up again. - **Uploads no longer stall** when Trio is in the background, and E3 alarms are fixed. - The 365 handshake retries if it fails, and the vibration toggle silences the transmitter properly. - **More is sent to Eversense DMS** to help their support team: app information, transmitter battery history and glucose logs. ### AccuChek SmartGuide - **Trio warns you if your sensor model is not supported.** - Calibration screens were tidied up. ### Both AccuChek and Eversense - **Warm-up and expiry now show on the Home screen** ([#1592](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1592)), the same way they do for other sensors. - **Calibrations are stored as fingersticks** ([#1472](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1472)). A reading you enter yourself is now saved as a manual glucose entry – the red drop on the chart – rather than being mixed in with sensor readings. ### Dexcom - **Sensor states can be sent to Nightscout** ([#1420](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1420)). A new switch under **Nightscout → Upload**, off by default, posts a note such as "CGM: sensorFailed" whenever a G6 or G7 reading arrives without usable glucose. Each state is noted once per occurrence. --- ## In the App - **The basal rate on the Home chart is right again** ([#1556](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1556)). It no longer shows a temp basal that has already been cancelled – for example after switching to Basal Testing. It also shows your scheduled rate before the pump has any history, marks a manual temp basal as manual, and says when delivery is suspended. - **Override presets no longer crash the Adjustments screen** ([#1571](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1571)). Presets saved by older builds with missing or unusual values were enough to bring the screen down. - **The bolus keyboard stops covering the field you are typing in** ([#1434](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1434)), along with some related scrolling problems in the Treatments view. - **Settings hints are no longer cut off** in longer translations ([#1408](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1408)), and the two Home grid toggles no longer touch each other at small text sizes ([#1575](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/pull/1575)). - Updated translations across Trio and its drivers, from our Crowdin and Lokalise contributors. --- ## Upgrade Notes ### From `1.0.1` or `1.0` **If you use a Libre 3 / 3+, pair your sensor again straight after updating** – see the note at the top of these release notes. That is the only thing you have to do. Everything else carries over: no settings change, no migration, no onboarding. If you are a new Trio user, check your alarm sound settings, as the defaults for new installs changed. ### From `0.8.4` Read the [`1.0` release notes](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0) – everything in their upgrade section still applies to you, including checking your alarm settings and your App Diagnostics preference. Your configuration, therapy settings, history and device connections carry over; there is no onboarding wizard and no settings reset. ### From `0.2.x` Read the [`0.7.0` upgrade notes](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v0.7.0#upgrade-notes) and the [Migration Guide on TrioDocs](https://triodocs.org/configuration/migration/trio-02x-migration/) first, then the [`1.0` notes](https://github.com/nightscout/Trio/releases/tag/v1.0). ### From `1.0.1.x` (`dev`) You are already running this code. No action needed beyond switching to `main`. --- ## A Note From The Trio Team **Trio has not been reviewed by the FDA or any other regulatory body.** Nothing in these notes is medical advice; if a change here affects how you manage your diabetes, talk it through with your care team. --- ## Contributors **Code:** @dnzxy, @bastiaanv, @ps2, @marionbarker, @bjorkert, @kingst, @LiroyvH, @aditmer, @jwoglom, @kristinkand, @lolzivkovic **Drivers:** the OmnipodKit, EversenseKit, MedtrumKit, DanaKit, AccuChekKit, LibreLoop, RoundWhiteDiscKit and LoopKit maintainers – see the submodule pull requests for full credit. **Translators:** Crowdin and Lokalise contributors across all supported languages. ---
